video_title: Can The Clippers Ever Recover?! | Rachel Nichols and Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' severe punishment after their year-long investigation
quotes.excerpt: five first-round picks, docked by the LA Clippers. Steve Ballmer, the owner, he gets suspended for a year.
quotes.quote: The Clippers last week were punished severely by the NBA in the aftermath of the results being revealed of this year-long investigation: five first-round picks, docked by the LA Clippers. Steve Ballmer, the owner, he gets suspended for a year. Gillian Zucker, she gets suspended for a year. Lawrence Frank, he gets suspended for six months, $30 million fine for the LA Clippers.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Reporters' frustration over being deceived by the Clippers
quotes.excerpt: I've heard from a lot of reporters who have expressed real frustration at what they were told.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Since this all came out, I've heard from a lot of reporters who have expressed real frustration at what they were told by the Clippers. They feel deceived by the Clippers. I was too far gone, I was pretty close-minded on this from jump, because to me, my thought was if it looks like a duck and it walks like a duck, it's probably a duck.

text_blocks.speaker: Rachel Nichols
text_blocks.text: I just said, hey, we got to wait and see what the investigation happens, right?

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Rachel Nichols on the betrayal of long-term professional relationships
quotes.excerpt: it's a bummer to have people you've known for 20, 25 years who looked you in the eye
quotes.quote: It's a bummer to have people you've known for 20, 25 years who looked you in the eye and lied to your face. Because I want everyone out there to think about people they've known for 25 years. If that person looked at you and said, hey man, this just isn't what you think it is, wait for the investigation, you'd be like, all right, I'm at least going to give them the benefit of the doubt. I never did that, and I don't think a lot of people ever did that. The benefit of the doubt was, well, let's wait and see. Let's see what people who, in Pablo Torre's words, with more subpoena power than I have, can find out. And they sure as heck did.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Questions regarding the Clippers' leadership and future direction
quotes.excerpt: who's running the organization right now? Where are they going to go in terms of direction?
quotes.quote: Where they go from here is twofold. We're going to talk about the basketball part, but also I have questions, who's running the organization right now? I don't know. Where are they going to go in terms of direction of the team? You brought up last week, does Ballmer sell the team? There are some really, really, really big picture questions here beyond the nuts and bolts of sort of how do they manage draft picks for the next couple years.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Ty Lue's uncertain future with the Clippers' rebuild
quotes.excerpt: do you talk to Ty Lue at some point? Do you want to be part of a rebuild?
quotes.quote: Do you talk to Ty Lue at some point? Do you want to be here? Do you want to be part of what's going to be a decade-long rebuild? I mean, he's got three years left on his contract. Do you want to be part of that?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' loss of draft capital and trade flexibility
quotes.excerpt: they lose their next five first-round draft picks, that not only mitigates their ability to get good
quotes.quote: They lose their next five first-round draft picks, that not only mitigates their ability to get good young players, it almost destroys their ability to make a trade of any kind of particular meaning. If you're that front office, how are you operating in the immediate future? Obviously you want to close this deal for Kawhi Leonard because you want to try to get those two first-round picks, the swap. You want to start to rebuild some of that draft capital.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The uncertainty of long-term planning in the Clippers' front office
quotes.excerpt: I just don't know how much long-term planning is done by who right now.
quotes.quote: I just don't know how much long-term planning is done by who right now. Are you planning for the next two years? You planning for the next five years? You planning for the next seven years? I think you just trying to basically bottom out. You don't control your picks, you don't benefit from being bad the way some of these teams that have been tanking over the last three or four years do, because other people have your picks or your picks don't exist anymore.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: Toronto's likely adherence to the original Kawhi Leonard trade terms
quotes.excerpt: I have heard only that Toronto is going to honor the deal as constructed.
quotes.quote: I have heard only that Toronto is going to honor the deal as constructed. I haven't heard anything else, but they certainly don't have to. And it would be interesting to see whether they, this hasn't gone as of you and I sitting here, this hasn't gone through yet. It would be interesting to see if there's been any pick-up in conversation of, well, actually we'd like this, or how about this, or one less of that.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Raptors' animosity toward the Clippers over the Kawhi trade
quotes.excerpt: the Raptors, they hate the Clippers. It's the same front office, yes, over this player
quotes.quote: I think that if there was one team that was going to do it, it would be Toronto. The Raptors, they hate the Clippers. It's the same front office, yes, over this player and how these decisions set them back. I don't know if they were ever really in the mix to resign Kawhi Leonard back in those days. Was he going to go to LA always, Lakers or Clippers? Probably, but they had meetings and they were, yeah, the Clippers clearly broke the rules to get him, to keep him.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA's strict stance on honoring trade agreements
quotes.excerpt: if Adam Silver along the way gives one of these picks back, that move will be jumped on
quotes.quote: Now, if Adam Silver along the way gives one of these picks back, that move will be jumped on and dissected in a way it wasn't during the Stern era. And I'm curious if you think that the difference in sort of where we are in life and the sports media cycle is going to influence whether that type of thing happens beyond just what the Clippers do or don't do.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' need to become a 'receptacle' for bad contracts
quotes.excerpt: you have got to be a receptacle for bad contracts in order to get a draft pick back
quotes.quote: They've got to act like the Wizards have acted, like the Thunder have acted, like the Nets have acted. You have got to be a receptacle for bad contracts in order to get a draft pick back in return. If some team's out there and says, oh god, we've got to get this guy off our books, we'll sweeten the offer with a first-round pick, that's who the Clippers are for at least the next five years.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' draft pick situation as a cautionary tale
quotes.excerpt: the most recent case that kind of compares to this a little bit is the Timberwolves
quotes.quote: We all know that the most recent case that kind of compares to this a little bit is the Timberwolves, the Joe Smith. There actually was an email that says we are going to do this for X, right? That was during the David Stern era, five first-round draft picks. And then slowly over time, they got one back, then they got, you know, another one back a year, a year and a half later, I think something like that. That was a different time. That was not when the internet was going crazy the way it is.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The misconception that Nikola Jokic lacks competitiveness
quotes.excerpt: I think it is a huge misconception around basketball that Nikola Jokic is not interested in winning
quotes.quote: I think it is a huge misconception around basketball that Nikola Jokic is not interested in winning championships and is not competitive. He is absolutely interested in winning NBA titles and is competitive because he could not play at the level he is with the dedication it requires unless he was. So, that's the first thing. I think he wants to stay around and I think he wants to win again.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The front office's failure to build around Nikola Jokic
quotes.excerpt: I think that it's a shame for the Denver Nuggets fans that they have to go through this
quotes.quote: I think that it's a shame for the Denver Nuggets fans that they have to go through this and this uncertainty and these question marks. But for the front office, I say good. Good that you have these uncertainty, good that you're getting a little nervous. Be better, because it is just a crying shame that they have wasted so much of the prime of one of the best players we have seen in a very long time.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Nuggets' roster regression during the offseason
quotes.excerpt: this offseason, the Nuggets got worse. They lose Peyton Watson and that sign-and-trade deal
quotes.quote: This offseason, the Nuggets got worse. They lose Peyton Watson and that sign-and-trade deal. They lose Tim Hardaway Jr., good player off the bench for them. They add DeMar DeRozan, good player still back end of his career. Spencer Dinwiddie is back, Julian Strawther is still there, Jonas Valanciunas is gone. They still have one of the best starting lineups in the NBA. But they have consistently had one of the best starting lineups in the NBA. Their problem in the last couple of years has been a lack of depth and they continue to hemorrhage talent.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The Nuggets' financial mistakes regarding Tim Connelly
quotes.excerpt: how much money do you think they didn't want to pay Tim Connelly after that title
quotes.quote: How much money do you think they didn't want to pay Tim Connelly after that title and that he went to Minnesota and the success he's had working his absolute magic for the Timberwolves? How much money have they ended up having to spend in luxury tax and just losing out on money in playoff rounds and playoff money and possibly another title and things like that? I just there is no amount of money Connelly could have wanted that would have equaled out what they, when they let him walk out the door, what they've had to spend since.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The Nuggets' failure to retain championship-level talent
quotes.excerpt: Sam Presti knew that if he made that offer to Jones and that he required the Nuggets
quotes.quote: Sam Presti knew that if he made that offer to Jones and that he required the Nuggets to do these backflips, they would be a weaker team when Oklahoma City met them in the playoffs and they absolutely will be. And that's just a level of front-officing, man. And I don't know why they didn't want to do everything they could to keep Tim Connelly in that front office, but they didn't. He went to the Timberwolves and look what he's done there since.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The difficulty of repeating as NBA champions
quotes.excerpt: it's extremely hard to repeat in this league with the way the rules and everything else are
quotes.quote: It's extremely hard to repeat in this league with the way the rules and everything else are right now. So the spotlight on the Minnesota Timberwolves getting their picks back was not considered like a huge talking point on SportsCenter every night.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: The Nuggets' obligation to maximize their championship window
quotes.excerpt: I feel like they've got to take the pick that they got in this Peyton Watson deal
quotes.quote: I feel like they've got to take the pick that they got in this Peyton Watson deal and actually turn it into something this year. And that is why my urgency level is probably higher than yours is. Not because I think Nikola Jokic is pounding on anyone's desk and threatening to walk away, but I just think that you have an obligation to try to build a better team around this guy because I promise you, it's not getting better from here.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: The Nuggets' need to upgrade their bench depth
quotes.excerpt: you've got to find some way to upgrade that bench before the trade deadline
quotes.quote: You've got to find some way to upgrade that bench before the trade deadline. Because you're not beating one of these top-tier teams. Look, I think they can beat, look when Jokic is on his game, like he saw those games the end of the regular season against the Spurs, like they can be competitive, they can win, they can beat Oklahoma City. But you can't just have a starting lineup alone. As much as I like DeMar DeRozan at this stage of his career and the player that he is, he kind of is what he is, right? He's a good, solid 7-8 guy off that bench, can play multiple positions, make you a mid-range shot, get you a bucket when you need it. He is a valuable addition to that team, but it's not enough. They don't have enough right now. They've got to find a way to get enough before that trade deadline.
